paragraphs.source_en: the analogous question. It says that if you examine the way the coin is set spinning with adequate precision, you can, in principle, predict whether it will land heads or tails. On closer inspection, then, precisely one out come is determined by details you initially overlooked. The same cannot be said in quantum physics. Decoherence allows quantum probabilities to be interpreted much like classical ones, but does not provide any finer details that select one of the many possible outcomes to actually happen. Much in the spirit of Bohr, some physicists believe that searching for such an explanation of how a single, definite outcome arises is misguided. These physicists argue that quantum mechanics, with its updating to include decoherence, is a sharply formulated theory whose predictions account for the behavior of laboratory measuring devices.
